newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo, Hungarian firms sign 45-mln mark deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo, Hungarian firms sign 45-mln mark deal - paper.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Industrija Motora Rakovica (IMR) and Dinara firms have signed a deal with Hungary's Raba for development and production of medium-powered diesel engines, Belgrade newspapers reported Friday.
The long-term cooperation deal, worth an estimated 45 million German marks, provides for the production of D-10 diesel engines and exchange of parts and components, the Vecernje Novosti paper said.
In the first stage, IMR will use RABA parts to instal engines that meet world standards and ecological requirements, Raba general manager Zalan Barnabas was quoted as saying.
Later the Rakovica firm will begin producing parts and complete engines, he added.
No-one at IMR or Dinara was available for comment.
IMR assembles engines for the needs of Yugoslav firms such as FAP, 14. oktobar, Ikarbus, Neobus, Zmaj, IMT, MIN, Sever, Radoje Dakic and for shipyards.

In the 20-year period of cooperation with Raba, interrupted by international sanctions against rump Yugoslavia, goods worth $1.5 billion were exchanged between Yugoslavia and Hungary, Dinara director Dinara Sava Corovic was quoted as saying.
